correctness.rationale: Every positive support is a vertex cover, and the matching gives size at least n. The size-n covers are exactly the canonical staircase covers. Interior staircase covers are total but have zeros on both bipartition sides, forcing two defenders; the leaves force those defenders to be a_1 and b_n. A size-(n+1) equality support has one defender, hence all zeros lie on one side; totality forces the added universal vertex and leaf defense forces the defender. The all-positive equality occurs only at n=2. Exhaustive verification through n=7 matches the theorem exactly.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves the optimum structure of an established domination parameter on the canonical twin-free chain family. It connects maximum independent sets, minimum vertex covers, total support, and the two leaf-forced Roman defenders in one exact classification. The n+1 staircase count for all n>=3 is a natural family-level invariant and a useful contrast with the complete-bipartite benchmark.
